speaker: muhammad
text: Think not that any good act is contemptible, though it be but your brother’s coming to you with an open countenance and good humour.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: muhammad
text: Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and free the captive if he be unjustly bound.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: muhammad
text: Give the labourer his wage before his perspiration be dry.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: muhammad
text: He is not strong or powerful who throws people down, but he is strong who withholds himself from anger.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: muhammad
text: Fear God in respect of animals: ride them when they are fit to be ridden, and get off when they are tired.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: muhammad
text: Whoso consoleth one in misfortune, for him is a reward equal to that of the sufferer.
credit: tr. in Stanley Lane-Poole, The Speeches and Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad, 1882
note: a saying handed down by tradition (hadith), from Lane-Poole’s selection

speaker: gautama-buddha
text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
note: a verse of the Dhammapada, which Buddhist tradition gives as the Buddha’s words

speaker: gautama-buddha
text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
note: a verse of the Dhammapada, which Buddhist tradition gives as the Buddha’s words

speaker: gautama-buddha
text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
note: a verse of the Dhammapada, which Buddhist tradition gives as the Buddha’s words

speaker: laozi
text: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
note: from the Tao Te Ching, which tradition gives to Laozi

speaker: laozi
text: The highest excellence is like (that of) water. The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things, and in its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike.
note: from the Tao Te Ching, which tradition gives to Laozi

speaker: laozi
text: The tree which fills the arms grew from the tiniest sprout; the tower of nine storeys rose from a (small) heap of earth; the journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
note: from the Tao Te Ching, which tradition gives to Laozi

speaker: moses
text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD…
note: as the Book of Deuteronomy records his words to Israel
licence: Public domain; Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0

speaker: moses
text: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live…
note: as the Book of Deuteronomy records his words to Israel
licence: Public domain; Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0

speaker: moses
text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
note: as the Book of Deuteronomy records his words to Israel
